edinburgh_holyrood_steward.text: Welcome to Holyroodhouse, the King's official home in Scotland, at the foot of the Royal Mile.
Mary, Queen of Scots, lived here from 1561 to 1567. Her rooms are in the oldest tower.
The Great Gallery has 89 portraits of Scottish kings, painted in the 1680s. Not all of the kings were real. Some were enthusiastic guesses.
Next door are the ruins of Holyrood Abbey, founded in 1128. Legend says King David saw a stag with a cross between its antlers. Hence Holy Rood.

edinburgh_holyrood_gardener.text: Arthur's Seat is just behind us, an extinct volcano with a view. The hedges here have more opinions than I do.

then.text: Back across the road for me. The Parliament's coffee is better than mine, and so are its arguments.

else.text: {greeting} I'm a researcher at the Scottish Parliament, across the road. I come over here for the quiet.
Scotland's old parliament stopped sitting with the Union of 1707. In a 1997 referendum 74% voted for a new one, and it first met in 1999.
There are 129 MSPs. They make the laws on health, schools, justice and more. Scots law and the courts were always Scotland's own, even before 1999.
Wales got its Assembly and Northern Ireland its Assembly at much the same time. England's laws are still made at Westminster. That's devolution.
Noted in the Gazetteer, under How these isles work.
